story: I paid Rs 5,10,000 to an interior designer in Pune on 1 July 2026; work never started and no refund.

timeline.event: Paid Rs 5,10,000 to an interior designer in Pune
timeline.user_words: I paid Rs 5,10,000 to an interior designer in Pune on 1 July 2026

evidence: Payment of Rs 5,10,000 to interior designer
missing: Date of refund refusal or demand

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 01 Jul 2028 (601 days left). This counts 2 years from 01 Jul 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 510,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with a Rs 200 fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You are a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. You paid Rs 5,10,000 for interior design services that were never provided, and you are entitled to a refund. You can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission in Pune, which has jurisdiction over your amount. The filing fee is Rs 200.

claims.text: You are a consumer because you hired an interior designer for a personal home service for consideration paid.
Not providing the agreed interior design service is a 'deficiency' in service.
Refusing to refund your Rs 5,10,000 after not providing the service is an 'unfair trade practice'.
You must file your complaint within two years from the date you paid, which is 1 July 2028.
The District Commission in Pune has jurisdiction because that is where the service provider works and where the cause of action arose.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to register your grievance.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step that can sometimes resolve the issue without needing a formal complaint.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the interior designer demanding a refund of Rs 5,10,000.
next_steps.why: This documents your attempt to resolve the issue directly before going to the Commission.

next_steps.action: File a consumer complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in with the District Commission in Pune.
next_steps.why: This is the formal legal step to get a refund order from the Commission.

support.text: You are a consumer because you hired an interior designer for a personal home service for consideration paid.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as any person who hires or avails of any service for consideration paid, promised, partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment. The sentence states the person hired an interior designer for a personal home service for consideration paid, which directly matches the definition.

support.text: Not providing the agreed interior design service is a 'deficiency' in service.
support.reason: The law text defines 'deficiency' as any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service. Not providing the agreed interior design service is a shortcoming/inadequacy in the performance of service, which directly matches the definition.

support.text: Refusing to refund your Rs 5,10,000 after not providing the service is an 'unfair trade practice'.
support.reason: The law text defines 'unfair trade practice' in clause (viii) as refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days. The sentence mentions Rs 5,10,000 but the law text does not mention any specific amount cap or threshold. However, the core issue is that the law text requires the refusal to be 'after selling goods or rendering services' - the sentence states 'after not providing the service', which is a logical contradiction (you cannot refuse to refund after not providing the service if the service was never provided; the law text contemplates refusal after services have been rendered). More critically, the law text specifies a thirty-day period for refund, but the sentence does not mention any time limit, which is a required element under the law text. The sentence adds no time limit, amount cap, right, penalty or condition - but actually the sentence fails to include the time limit element that the law text requires ('within a period of thirty days' or 'within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt'). Since the sentence does not contain this required time limit element, it does not fully match the legal rule.

support.text: You must file your complaint within two years from the date you paid, which is 1 July 2028.
support.reason: The law text states complaints must be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen, not from the date the person paid. The sentence incorrectly states the filing period is 'from the date you paid' rather than 'from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.' The sentence also computes a specific date (1 July 2028) which is not in the law text and appears to be an invented date. The law text does not specify any particular filing date or allow computation from the payment date as the starting point.

support.text: The District Commission in Pune has jurisdiction because that is where the service provider works and where the cause of action arose.
support.reason: The law text states a complaint may be instituted in a District Commission within whose jurisdiction (a) the opposite party ordinarily resides or carries on business or has a branch office or personally works for gain, OR (c) the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises. The sentence states the District Commission in Pune has jurisdiction because that is where the service provider works (matches clause (a)) and where the cause of action arose (matches clause (c)).

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
